ImageDescription.value:
Spodoptera eridania - Southern armyworm. A pest in southern parts of the U.S. mostly Florida. Defoliator of tomatoes and other crops. Not a candidate for the insect Miss Universe contest...or is is? I think close up there is a lot of beauty in this series of life history shots, but that is my personal opinion. Specimens provided by Benzon Research.

All photographs are public domain, feel free to download and use as you wish.

Photography Information: Canon Mark II 5D, Zerene Stacker, Stackshot Sled, 65mm Canon MP-E 1-5X macro lens, Twin Macro Flash in Styrofoam Cooler, F5.0, ISO 100, Shutter Speed 200

Want some Useful Links to the Techniques We Use? Well now here you go Citizen:


Basic USGSBIML set up: www.youtube.com/watch?v=S-_yvIsucOY

USGSBIML Photoshopping Technique: Note that we now have added using the burn tool at 50% opacity set to shadows to clean up the halos that bleed into the black background from "hot" color sections of the picture. www.youtube.com/watch?v=Bdmx_8zqvN4

PDF of Basic USGSBIML Photography Set Up: ftp://ftpext.usgs.gov/pub/er/md/laurel/Droege/How%20to%20Take%20MacroPhotographs%20of%20Insects%20BIML%20Lab2.pdf

Google Hangout Demonstration of Techniques: plus.google.com/events/c5569losvskrv2nu606ltof8odo or www.youtube.com/watch?v=4c15neFttoU

ImageDescription.value: Hydrachnidia, also known as "water mites", Hydrachnidiae, Hydracarina or Hydrachnellae, are among the most abundant and diverse groups of benthic arthropods, composed of 6,000 described species from 57 families. This specimen was found in a city pond in the city of Rakvere in Estonia

Categories.value: Simocephalus|Self-published work|Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation|Featured pictures of animals in Estonia|Featured pictures of Lääne-Viru County|Featured pictures by Janek Lass

ImageDescription.value: Simocephalus sp. are 3-4 mm in length, round animals that are covered in a bivalve carapace. The head, which contains a single compound eye, is not covered by this carapace but instead is surrounded by a hood. This specimen was found in a city pond in the city of Rakvere in Estonia

Categories.value: Ostracoda|Self-published work|Featured pictures of animals in Estonia|Featured pictures of Lääne-Viru County|Focus stacking images of Crustacea|Featured pictures by Janek Lass

ImageDescription.value: Ostracods are crustaceans up to 2 mm long that can be found in all kinds of water bodies: both sea and fresh water, small puddles, ponds, large lakes, rivers, springs, groundwater, etc. They prefer to operate in water close to the bottom, but especially in the sea, some species can also be found in the upper water layer. Already from the shore of the pond, you can see these miniature bean-shaped animals climbing or swimming in the shallow water. About 5,700 species of crustaceans are known in world, 93 have been found in Estonian waters, but the existence of about 100 species is assumed. These specimens were found in a temporary water body near the Estonian town of Rakvere
